title: Three pillars
hook: Simon the Just: the world stands on Torah, worship and acts of kindness (Pirkei Avot 1:2)
tomorrow: if i'm only for myself, what am i? who asked that, and why?

segments.voice: Yesterday, the Japji's last verse: air the guru, water the father, earth the mother, and many set free together. Air, water, earth.

A wobbly café table has four legs. A three-legged stool never wobbles, even on a crooked floor. So, which three things hold up the world? An old Jewish book of sayings, Pirkei Avot, gives an answer in its second saying. Simon the Just, called one of the last of the Great Assembly, used to say: the world stands on three things. On Torah, the teaching. On avodah, the service of worship in the Temple. And on gemilut chasadim, acts of loving-kindness. Three legs. A steady world. Except for one problem.
screen: `THE STOOL THAT NEVER WOBBLES.` → `SIMON THE JUST.` → `TORAH, WORSHIP, KINDNESS.` → `ONE PROBLEM.`

segments.voice: Here's the puzzle. One of the three legs was the Temple service, the offerings in Jerusalem. And the Temple was destroyed. So what is the world standing on now? A story from Avot de-Rabbi Natan answers it. Rabban Yohanan ben Zakkai was walking out of Jerusalem with his student, Rabbi Joshua, and they passed the Temple in ruins. Joshua cried out: woe to us, the place where Israel's wrongs were atoned for is gone. Yohanan said: my son, don't grieve. We have another atonement just like it. Which? Acts of loving-kindness. And he quoted the prophet Hosea, in the King James words: "For I desired mercy, and not sacrifice." Look at the Hebrew. The word Hosea uses for mercy is chesed, the same word inside gemilut chasadim. The third leg was holding the weight all along. This is a real turn in Jewish life. The rabbis taught that prayer is the service of the heart, and that kindness carries what the altar used to carry. It's one reason visiting the sick, feeding a guest and comforting mourners count as holy work in Judaism, not as extras next to it. When one pillar falls, the others take the load.
screen: `ONE LEG WAS THE TEMPLE.` · `WALKING PAST THE RUINS.` · `I DESIRED MERCY, NOT SACRIFICE.` · then, large: `KINDNESS CARRIES THE WEIGHT.`

segments.voice: Choose one person who could use an act of kindness this week, and name, to yourself, the kind thing you could do. Then name what usually stops you, the awkwardness, the busy day, and decide when and how you'll do it anyway: if this happens, then I'll do that.
Three pillars: Torah, worship and acts of loving-kindness, the three things Simon the Just says the world stands on.
Hold onto this: three pillars, and the kindness one still standing. Day one of the sayings of the Fathers.

howItsDone: Jews study Pirkei Avot, the Sayings of the Fathers, often on Shabbat afternoons in the weeks after Passover; acts of loving-kindness, such as visiting the sick and comforting mourners, are treated as religious duties.
